subject: Neurolytics reserved capacity options and ramp scenarios
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tom Greene <tom.greene@neurolytics.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 15:24:00 -0700
Subject: Reserved capacity options and ramp scenarios for Neurolytics

Hi Tom,

Thanks again for the demo last week — excited about how Neurolytics plans to use embeddings + multi-turn generation for clinician summarization. Per our conversation, attached are three reserve options that balance cost, latency, and predictable throughput. High-level summary below; full numbers + burn estimates are in the attached PDF and spreadsheet.

1) Pilot Lane (3-month onboarding)
- Minimum reserved: 8x A100-sim (32GB-equivalent)
- Burst: up to 16x on demand for spikes
- Ramp schedule: start at 8 for month 1, 12 in month 2, evaluate for month 3
- Use case: model evaluation, infra smoke tests, short-retention KV cache

2) Production Growth
- Minimum reserved: 30x A100-sim + 10x T4-style inference pool
- Ramp schedule: 30 at activation, +10 in month 3, +10 optional in month 6
- SLOs: 99.95%% regionally for token latency (P50/P95 targets included in PDF)
- Features: prefix/KV warm cache, auto-batching with adjustable latency targets, model pinning for rollouts

3) Anchored Enterprise
- Minimum reserved: 60x A100-sim + 20x T4-style inference nodes + 4x L4 for low-latency routes
- Ramp schedule: 30 initial activation, 60 by month 4 with scheduled warmup windows
- Includes surge corridor and cross-region fallback for DR

Options and tradeoffs to consider: quantized model variants for cheaper token cost, mixed fleet to keep generates fast while offloading heavy batch jobs to lower-cost instances, and warm-cache credits during onboarding. We can also structure a stepped commitment (months 0–3 trial pricing, then committed floor).

Attachments: neurolytics_reserve_options_v1.pdf (proposal, SLOs, pricing bands), neurolytics_onramp_costs.xlsx (month-by-month burn + run-rate).

Next steps: which lane looks closest? If you want, we can run a 2-week canary with the Pilot Lane and pre-provision warm cache (we charge a small warmup fee that can be applied to the first month). Also happy to schedule a technical deep-dive with our infra team to walk through KV caching and warm-start behavior.

Best,
Monica Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Tom Greene <tom.greene@neurolytics.ai>

Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 09:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity options and ramp scenarios for Neurolytics

Thanks Monica — this is very helpful. A couple quick clarifying questions before we send this to procurement: 

- For the Production Growth lane, what is the guaranteed minimum P95 token latency for embedding requests (single-turn)? Our SLA target is sub-200ms P95 for embeddings during normal load.
- Does the warm-cache credit cover pre-populating common patient prefixes, or is that an engineering task we need to own?
- Can you provide a ballpark monthly cost for the Production Growth lane (30 A100-sim + 10 T4 pool) and the Anchored Enterprise lane? It helps to have a month 1 vs month 6 delta.

Also compliance: procurement needs your SOC2/ISO docs and a short note on data retention/tenant isolation for Private deployments. If you can drop those or point me to where they live, that'd be ideal.

If it's easier, happy to jump on a 30-min call.

—Tom
Tom Greene
VP Product, Neurolytics
tom.greene@neurolytics.ai
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: 
Date: Sat, 14 Mar 2026 10:18:00 -0700
Subject: FW: Reserved capacity options and ramp scenarios for Neurolytics

Ben / Karthik — forwarding Tom's clarifying questions (below). He wants: P95 embedding latency guarantee for the Production Growth lane, confirmation about warm-cache scope, monthly cost examples, and SOC2/ISO + data retention note for Private. Procurement will likely need the doc pack.

My suggested responses / internal notes:
- P95 embedding: we **can** commit to sub-200ms P95 for embeddings if we route embeddings to the L4/fast lane (or L4-equivalent) and reserve a small low-latency pool in front of the A100s. For the Growth lane we proposed 10x T4-style nodes; swap 4 of those to L4 (or equivalent) and reserve them for embeddings to hit sub-200ms P95. We should call this out as a "latency carve-out" in the SLA.
- Warm-cache credits: engineering will pre-populate prefixes we agree on as part of onboarding; however, long-tail prefill is customer's responsibility. We should offer up to 100k tokens of prefill as part of the onboarding credit, then ramp to customer-funded prefill.
- Cost: attach quick sheet with month 1 (activation + warmup) and steady-state run-rate. Use conservative GPU-hour pricing and add 12% infra ops premium for reserve.
- SOC2/ISO: point to compliance pack link + offer to provide an extracted packet for procurement (redact internal notes).

Action: Ben — can you run numbers for 30A100 + mix-with-4L4 and produce: month1 cost / month3 cost / month6 steady-state? Karthik — confirm feasibility of carving out low-latency L4 pool and whether autoscaler can honor the carve-out without stealing from compute credits.

Thanks — I'll pull the compliance links and draft Tom a response next week.

M

Subject: Re: Reserved capacity options and ramp scenarios for Neurolytics

Hi Tom — replying with answers and an updated cost sheet attached. Thanks for the quick follow-up.

1) Latency guarantee (Production Growth)
We can guarantee sub-200ms P95 for single-turn embeddings in the Production Growth lane by reserving a 4-node low-latency pool (L4-equivalent) that fronts embedding routes. We'll add a latency carve-out to the SLA: embeddings routed to the low-latency pool will have a P95 target of <= 200ms under normal load (up to the reserved pool capacity). If you want a 99th percentile guarantee we can discuss additional reservation.

2) Warm-cache scope
Onboarding includes up to 100k tokens prefill for agreed prefixes (our infra team will coordinate a prefill run with your team). Anything beyond that is measurable work and will be billed separately or applied to additional onboarding credits.

3) Cost examples (attached spreadsheet)
- Production Growth (month 1 activation + warmup): $128,400
- Production Growth (steady-state month 3): $95,700/month
- Anchored Enterprise (month 1): $255,000
- Anchored Enterprise (steady-state month 6): $180,200/month
Numbers include reserved GPU hours, warmup credits, 12%% infra ops premium, and a 10%% committed discount on steady-state. Detailed line items are in neurolytics_onramp_costs.xlsx.

4) Compliance and procurement packet
I've included a link to our compliance pack and attached a redacted SOC2 summary. If procurement needs an extracted packet (SOC2 + ISO + data retention overview + network isolation diagram) we can produce that within 48 hours.

Next steps:
- If the Growth lane with a 4-node low-latency carve-out sounds right, I can generate a canary SOW and a DocuSign packet for signature.
- Suggest a 30-min technical call with our infra leads (Ben/Karthik) — propose Wed 17 Mar or Thu 18 Mar. What works for you?

Attachments: neurolytics_onramp_costs.xlsx (updated), neurolytics_reserve_options_v1.pdf (redline: latency carve-out)

Best,
